definition: The query likelihood model is a language model used in information retrieval.
details: A language model is constructed for each document in the collection. It is then possible to rank each document by the probability of specific documents given a query. This is interpreted as being the likelihood of a document being relevant given a query.

explainer.lead: The query likelihood model is a language model used in information retrieval that ranks documents by their probability given a query. It matters because it turns relevance ranking into a likelihood computation.

tiers.eli5: The system learns what words each document is likely to use, then ranks documents by how likely each one is to have produced your search.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers build a language model per document, then rank documents by the probability of the document given the query, read as the likelihood of relevance. A pitfall is that ranking depends on per-document language models, so collection size matters.
tiers.paperLevel: A language model is constructed for each document in the collection, and each document is ranked by the probability of the document given a query, interpreted as the likelihood of relevance.

explainer.example: With one language model per document, a query is scored against each model and documents are ordered by the resulting probability.
